name: euler2d_cylinder
title: Mach 6 cylinder: bow-shock stand-off and the carbuncle test (2D Euler, external_2d)

reference.quantity: Bow-shock stand-off distance / diameter (polar grid, carbuncle fix on)
reference.source: Billig, F. S. (1967), J. Spacecraft Rockets 4(6): Delta/R = 0.386 exp(4.67/M^2) for cylinders

reference.quantity: Bow-shock stand-off distance / diameter (Gmsh quad-dominant mesh, full front)
reference.source: Billig, F. S. (1967), J. Spacecraft Rockets 4(6): Delta/R = 0.386 exp(4.67/M^2) for cylinders

study.title: Runs
notes: Shock roughness: largest second difference of the shock radius between neighbouring grid rays, divided by the radial cell size (below 1: the front never jumps a whole cell between rays; it is similar with and without the fix here, so convergence is the clearer sign).

Carbuncle metric: peak-to-peak change of the volume-weighted pressure in the shock layer (box x = -0.45 to 0 D, y = 0 to 0.35 D) over the last 1,000 iterations, divided by its mean. It separates the runs clearly; the shock roughness above does not.
Without the fix (pure HLLC) the bow shock never settles on the shock-aligned grid: the residual stalls high; with the HLLE blend near the shock the run converges.
Inviscid, calorically perfect air (gamma = 1.4): a numerics test, not real Mach 6 air.
